defects.title: The error for several genes that are not in the model joins their names
defects.trigger: deleteModelGenes(model, {'g8', 'g9'}) with neither gene in model.genes
defects.observed: error 'Gene g8g9 not in model!' (line 108 concatenates geneList{~isInModel} without separator)
defects.expected: the missing gene names listed separately

defects.title: Deleting a gene that is already marked deleted appends the suffix again
defects.observed: model.genes{1} = 'g1_deleted_deleted' after the second call; constraints identical to the first call

notes: Placed in test/verifiedTests/analysis/testDeletionStudy (the deletion area folder; no test of src/analysis/deletion carries a 'Function under test' header). No testDeleteModelGenes.m existed and no legacy test tests only deleteModelGenes: grep finds calls in testMOMA.m, design/testSimpleOptKnock.m, design/testMultiProductionEnvelopeInorg.m and two tutorials, all as set-up for other functions, so a new file was written (III-Naming). Hand-built 6-reaction/5-gene model, every expected value derived by hand from the rules: single-gene rule, AND (complex), OR (isoenzymes; blocked only when both deleted), gene in two reactions (g2: AND reaction blocked, OR reaction kept), gene in no reaction, reaction with no rule, prefix names g1/g10 (each deletion affects only its own gene; 'g' is rejected), char and cell gene lists, default gene list (all genes), downRegFraction 0.5 (lb and ub halved), successive calls (a gene marked earlier still counts as absent), given rxnGeneMat (used as is; listed reaction with empty rule skipped), and the two by-design errors (missing gene, model without genes). Outputs checked: model genes/lb/ub/rxnGeneMat, hasEffect, constrRxnNames, deletedGenes (shape follows the input list: row for a row cell, column for the default). 100% line coverage (37 lines). Two cosmetic defects recorded (no lines left uncovered; the affected inputs are not called). Callees buildRxnGeneMat/findRxnIDs/changeRxnBounds behaved as expected; changeRxnBounds is called only when a reaction is constrained (not every input), so no extra edge.

No existing test (only tutorial_ecoliCoreModel_part1 calls it). Hand-built model with single-gene, AND and OR rules, prefix genes g1/g10, a reaction without rule, a missing reaction (printed by display() and dropped; order of the rest kept), only missing reactions (empty cell), char input (returns {{'g1';'g2'}}), and a given rxnGeneMat (read as is, not rebuilt). Output is a column cell with one column cell of gene names per found reaction, genes in model.genes order. 100% coverage (13 lines). Calls columnVector on every input but it is already tested, so no extra edge. Caller pFBA (src/analysis/parsimoniousFBA/pFBA.m) uses it normally.

defects.title: Every call that finds a junction stops on an undefined variable
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23) error "Unrecognized function or variable 'verbFlag'." at line 56; only calls finding no junction return (empty list)
defects.expected: {'x(c)'} (lines 55, 75-77), verbose listing of lines 56-69 behind an optional flag

notes: Reproduction (confirmed in MATLAB R2025a): model = struct('rxns', {{'A'; 'B'; 'C'}}, 'mets', {{'x[c]'}}, 'S', sparse([1 -1 -1]), 'c', [0; 0; 0], 'genes', {{'g1'; 'g2'; 'g3'}}, 'rules', {{'x(1)'; 'x(2)'; 'x(3)'}}); findMetabolicJunctions(model, 3)  -> Unrecognized function or variable 'verbFlag'. (line 56). findMetabolicJunctions(model, 4) returns {} (0x0). verbFlag is not an input, not assigned, and no verbFlag.m exists on the path, so the function can never return a non-empty result. No src caller (grep), so the quarantine blocks no other row. Calls parseMetNames on every input (already tested, no extra edge).
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: verbFlag at line 56 is never defined, so every call that finds a junction stops; no src caller)

defects.title: withComp is not passed to the recursive call, so common metabolites count as edges from the second order on
defects.trigger: findNeighborRxns(model, 'R2', true, 2, {'atp[c]', 'adp[c]'}, true) with the 3-reaction model in notes
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23) {'R1'; 'R2'; 'R3'}: line 150 omits withComp, the recursion appends the compartment again ('atp[c][c]') and links R1 to R3 through atp[c]/adp[c]
defects.expected: {'R1'; 'R2'}, as the equivalent withComp=false call (commonMets {'atp','adp'}) returns

notes: Reproduction (confirmed in MATLAB R2025a): model = struct('rxns', {{'R1'; 'R2'; 'R3'}}, 'mets', {{'a[c]'; 'b[c]'; 'atp[c]'; 'adp[c]'}}, 'S', sparse([-1 0 0; 1 -1 0; -1 0 -1; 1 0 1]), 'genes', {{'g1'}}, 'rules', {{'x(1)'; ''; ''}}); findNeighborRxns(model, 'R2', true, 2, {'atp[c]', 'adp[c]'}, true) -> {'R1';'R2';'R3'}; findNeighborRxns(model, 'R2', true, 2, {'atp', 'adp'}) -> {'R1';'R2'}; findNeighborRxns(model, 'R2', true, 1, {'atp[c]', 'adp[c]'}, true) -> {'R1'}. The defect is confined to the call form withComp = true with order >= 2 and asSingleArray = true (6 inputs). The only src caller, src/reconstruction/rBioNet/neighborRxn2data.m line 23, calls findNeighborRxns(model, rxnName) (2 inputs: withComp false, order 1), so it does NOT reach the defect. Probes of the other forms (per-metabolite cells, asSingleArray, order 2 without withComp, commonMets {''}, gene strings joined with '; ') matched hand-derived expectations, so the test can be written fully once line 150 passes withComp. Calls findMetIDs, findRxnIDs on every input (listed); parseMetNames only when withComp is false.
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: the recursive call at lines 149-150 passes commonMets but not withComp, so withComp true with order >= 2 treats common metabolites as links; seed NONE: neighborRxn2data passes two inputs)

defects.title: A gene list with no gene of the model stops with an error
defects.trigger: colorRxnsFromGenes(map, model, {'99'}) with model = struct('rxns', {{'R1'}}, 'genes', {{'10.1'}}, 'rules', {{'x(1)'}}); map = struct('rxnName', {{'R1'}})
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23) error 'Input A of class cell and input B of class double must be cell arrays of character vectors, unless one is a character vector.' from ismember at line 82: globalList stays [] (line 67), rxnName = unique([]) is double

notes: Reproduction (confirmed in MATLAB R2025a): model = struct('rxns', {{'R1'}}, 'genes', {{'10.1'}}, 'rules', {{'x(1)'}}); map = struct('rxnName', {{'R1'}}); colorRxnsFromGenes(map, model, {'99'}) -> ismember error (class cell vs double); colorRxnsFromGenes(map, model, {'10', '99'}) returns rxnColor {'FFFF0000'}, rxnWidth {8}. Found when the first full test failed on its 'no matching gene' section. A scratch copy of the full test without that section passed all other assertions (default RED/8, BLUE/3, GREEN with default width, '10' not matching '100.1', secondary reactant/product lines recoloured only when non-empty, given rxnGeneMat used as is), so the test can be restored once the defect is fixed (e.g. globalList = {} at line 67). No src caller (only tutorial_metabolicCartography_part2), so the quarantine blocks no other row. Lead may judge severity: if 'no listed gene in the model' is seen as a limitation instead of an error, the full test (minus that input) is ready to reinstate.
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: rxnName = unique(globalList) is [] (double) when no gene of the list is in the model, and ismember(newmap.rxnName, rxnName) at line 82 stops; a documented input that fails, error by research R5; the passing full test is kept in inventory/review/quarantined-full-tests/; no src caller)
